Tomato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a common fungal disease that causes dark spots with concentric rings on lower leaves, often spreading upward in warm, humid weather.

symptoms.name: Target-like spots
symptoms.explanation: Brown lesions with rings on older leaves.

symptoms.name: Yellowing
symptoms.explanation: Leaves may yellow around spots and drop early.

actions.step: Remove heavily infected lower leaves and destroy them (do not compost).
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Improve airflow by spacing plants and avoiding overhead watering.
Apply a fungicide labeled for early blight only if local extension guidance recommends it.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates and pre-harvest intervals.

Tomato___Early_blight.monitoring: Check lower leaves every few days; watch for new spots after rain.
Tomato___Early_blight.limitations: Similar spots can come from other fungi or physical damage; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Late blight spreads quickly in cool, wet conditions and can destroy foliage and fruit within days if not managed.

symptoms.name: Water-soaked patches
symptoms.explanation: Large irregular gray-green areas on leaves.

symptoms.name: White growth
symptoms.explanation: Fuzzy growth may appear on undersides in humid weather.

actions.step: Isolate affected plants if possible; remove severely infected plants.
actions.safety_note: Dispose away from the field; do not leave debris on soil.

actions.step: Avoid working in wet fields to limit spread.
Use protectant fungicides per local agricultural extension advice.
actions.safety_note: Wear protective equipment as required on the label.

Tomato___Late_blight.monitoring: Inspect daily during cool, rainy periods; act at first signs.
Tomato___Late_blight.limitations: Requires prompt action; photo-only diagnosis may miss early or mixed infections.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Early blight on potato causes dark lesions on leaves and can reduce tuber yield if left unmanaged.

symptoms.name: Dark leaf spots
symptoms.explanation: Angular to circular brown spots, often with rings.

symptoms.name: Defoliation
symptoms.explanation: Severe infection causes premature leaf drop.

actions.step: Rotate crops and use certified seed where available.
Maintain balanced fertility; avoid excess nitrogen that favors lush, susceptible foliage.
Consider fungicide programs aligned with local recommendations.
actions.safety_note: Follow label restrictions for food crops.

Potato___Early_blight.monitoring: Scout from tuber initiation through canopy closure.
Potato___Early_blight.limitations: Field history and weather strongly affect risk; confirm critical decisions locally.

Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab causes olive-green to dark scabby lesions on leaves and fruit, favored by spring moisture.

symptoms.name: Velvety spots
symptoms.explanation: Olive lesions on young leaves and fruit.

symptoms.name: Leaf curl
symptoms.explanation: Infected leaves may distort and fall.

actions.step: Remove fallen leaves in autumn to reduce overwintering spores.
Prune for light penetration and faster leaf drying.
Apply scab-targeted sprays per regional orchard calendar.
actions.safety_note: Respect re-entry and harvest intervals.

Apple___Apple_scab.monitoring: Watch new growth in wet springs; track weather-based infection periods if available.
Apple___Apple_scab.limitations: Fruit and leaf symptoms differ by variety; expert verification helps before spray decisions.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Common rust produces reddish-brown pustules on leaves, usually mid to late season depending on hybrid susceptibility.

symptoms.name: Rust pustules
symptoms.explanation: Small raised reddish-brown spots on both leaf surfaces.

symptoms.name: Yellow halos
symptoms.explanation: Chlorosis may surround heavy infections.

actions.step: Choose resistant hybrids for future plantings if rust is recurring.
Scout fields to distinguish common vs southern rust.
actions.safety_note: Misidentification changes urgency of control.

actions.step: Treat only when thresholds and economics justify it locally.
actions.safety_note: Follow label directions for grain crops.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.monitoring: Check mid-canopy leaves weekly in humid seasons.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.limitations: Rust species look similar in photos; lab or expert ID may be needed.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a fungal disease causing leaf spots, rotting fruit, and cankers on branches, spreading in warm, wet weather.

symptoms.name: Frog-eye spots
symptoms.explanation: Small purple spots that enlarge with tan centres and purple edges.

symptoms.name: Fruit rot
symptoms.explanation: Brown to black rot on fruit, often starting at the blossom end.

actions.step: Prune out dead wood, cankers, and mummified fruit and remove them from the orchard.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Rake and destroy fallen leaves and fruit.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Apple___Black_rot.monitoring: Check leaves and fruit every week from bloom; watch branches for sunken cankers.
Apple___Black_rot.limitations: Leaf spots can resemble other apple diseases; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease that needs both apple and nearby juniper/cedar trees to complete its life cycle.

symptoms.name: Orange spots
symptoms.explanation: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface in spring.

symptoms.name: Tufts underneath
symptoms.explanation: Small tube-like structures on the leaf underside later in the season.

actions.step: Remove nearby juniper or cedar galls where practical.
Rake and remove fallen infected leaves.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.monitoring: Watch new leaves in spring after wet weather; note any junipers within a few hundred metres.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.limitations: Other rusts and leaf spots look similar; confirm locally if unsure.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew is a fungal disease that coats young leaves and shoots with white powder, favoured by humid nights and dry days.

symptoms.name: White powder
symptoms.explanation: Fluffy white patches on leaves, often on young growth.

symptoms.name: Curled leaves
symptoms.explanation: Infected leaves may curl, pucker, or turn brittle.

actions.step: Prune to open the canopy and improve airflow.
Remove heavily infected shoots.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.monitoring: Check new shoots every few days during humid weather.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.limitations: Residue or dust can look like mildew; rub the leaf to check.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Gray leaf spot is a fungal disease of maize that forms long grey lesions between leaf veins, worst in warm, humid weather with residue left in the field.

symptoms.name: Rectangular lesions
symptoms.explanation: Narrow grey to tan lesions running parallel to the veins.

symptoms.name: Leaf death
symptoms.explanation: Lesions join together and whole leaves dry out.

actions.step: Rotate with a non-host crop and manage crop residue.
Use tolerant varieties in the next season.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.monitoring: Scout lower leaves weekly from knee height through grain fill.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.limitations: Other leaf blights look similar early; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Northern leaf blight is a fungal disease that forms long cigar-shaped lesions on maize leaves in moderate temperatures with heavy dew.

symptoms.name: Cigar-shaped lesions
symptoms.explanation: Long grey-green to tan lesions, several centimetres long.

symptoms.name: Lower leaves first
symptoms.explanation: Usually starts on lower leaves and moves upward.

actions.step: Rotate crops and manage infected residue.
Choose resistant hybrids for the next planting.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.monitoring: Check leaves weekly, especially before tasselling.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.limitations: Lesion shape helps, but lab confirmation may be needed for similar blights.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a fungal disease of grapes that causes leaf spots and turns berries into hard black mummies in warm, wet weather.

symptoms.name: Tan leaf spots
symptoms.explanation: Round tan spots with dark borders and tiny black dots.

symptoms.name: Mummified berries
symptoms.explanation: Berries shrivel into hard black raisins.

actions.step: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves from vines and ground.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Prune for airflow and sunlight in the canopy.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Grape___Black_rot.monitoring: Inspect leaves and young clusters weekly after rain.
Grape___Black_rot.limitations: Other grape leaf spots look similar; confirm locally if unsure.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Esca is a trunk disease of grapevines caused by wood-infecting fungi, showing as striped leaves and spotted berries.

symptoms.name: Tiger-stripe leaves
symptoms.explanation: Yellow or red bands between veins that dry out.

symptoms.name: Spotted berries
symptoms.explanation: Small dark spots on berries; vines may suddenly wilt.

actions.step: Mark affected vines and prune out dead wood in dry weather.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Protect large pruning wounds and disinfect tools between vines.
Ask an expert about trunk renewal for badly affected vines.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).monitoring: Track marked vines each season; symptoms can come and go between years.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).limitations: Leaf symptoms vary year to year; wood inspection by an expert confirms it.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Isariopsis leaf spot is a fungal disease causing dark irregular spots that can lead to early leaf drop in humid conditions.

symptoms.name: Dark irregular spots
symptoms.explanation: Brown to black angular spots on older leaves.

symptoms.name: Early leaf drop
symptoms.explanation: Badly affected leaves yellow and fall early.

actions.step: Remove fallen and infected leaves.
Improve airflow by canopy management.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.monitoring: Check older leaves weekly during humid weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.limitations: Several grape leaf spots look alike; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Citrus greening is a serious bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid. It has no cure and slowly kills trees.

symptoms.name: Blotchy mottle
symptoms.explanation: Uneven yellow blotches that do not match on both sides of the leaf.

symptoms.name: Poor fruit
symptoms.explanation: Small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays partly green.

actions.step: Report suspected trees to your local agricultural or plant protection office.
Control psyllids as advised by local experts.
actions.safety_note: Follow local guidance for any insecticide use.

actions.step: Remove confirmed infected trees as advised to protect nearby trees.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).monitoring: Inspect trees monthly for psyllids and new yellowing.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).limitations: Nutrient deficiency looks similar; lab testing is needed to confirm greening.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot causes small leaf spots, shot holes, and pitted fruit on peaches, spreading in warm, wet, windy weather.

symptoms.name: Shot holes
symptoms.explanation: Small angular spots whose centres drop out, leaving holes.

symptoms.name: Fruit pitting
symptoms.explanation: Small dark spots and cracks on the fruit skin.

actions.step: Choose tolerant varieties for new plantings.
Avoid overhead irrigation and prune for airflow.
Ask your extension office about copper-based sprays and timing.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.monitoring: Check leaves and young fruit after rainy, windy spells.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.limitations: Fungal shot hole looks similar; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot causes water-soaked spots on pepper leaves and fruit and spreads by splashing water and infected seed.

symptoms.name: Water-soaked spots
symptoms.explanation: Small dark spots, sometimes with yellow halos.

symptoms.name: Leaf drop
symptoms.explanation: Badly affected leaves yellow and drop, exposing fruit to sun.

actions.step: Remove infected plants and debris.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Avoid overhead watering and working with wet plants.
Use disease-free seed and rotate away from peppers and tomatoes.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.monitoring: Check leaves every few days in warm, wet weather.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.limitations: Several spot diseases look similar; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Late blight spreads fast in cool, wet weather and can destroy potato foliage and rot tubers within days.

symptoms.name: Water-soaked patches
symptoms.explanation: Dark, greasy-looking patches that spread quickly.

symptoms.name: White growth
symptoms.explanation: White fuzzy growth on the leaf underside in humid conditions.

actions.step: Remove and destroy badly affected leaves (do not compost).
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Avoid overhead watering and hill up soil to protect tubers.
Contact your extension office quickly; protective sprays may be needed.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Potato___Late_blight.monitoring: Check plants daily during cool, wet weather; act fast if it spreads.
Potato___Late_blight.limitations: Can be confused with early blight; rapid spread suggests late blight.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew coats squash leaves with white powder, weakening plants and reducing yield, especially in dry days with humid nights.

symptoms.name: White powder
symptoms.explanation: Round white powdery spots that spread across leaves.

symptoms.name: Yellowing
symptoms.explanation: Leaves yellow and dry out early.

actions.step: Remove the most affected older leaves.
Space plants for airflow and water at the base.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.monitoring: Check leaf tops and undersides twice a week.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.limitations: Residue can look similar; rub the leaf to check.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Leaf scorch is a fungal disease causing many small purple spots that merge until leaves look burnt.

symptoms.name: Purple spots
symptoms.explanation: Many small dark purple spots without pale centres.

symptoms.name: Scorched look
symptoms.explanation: Spots join and leaves dry up as if burnt.

actions.step: Remove infected old leaves after harvest.
Avoid overhead watering and keep beds weed-free.
Plant certified disease-free runners.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.monitoring: Check leaves weekly, especially in wet periods.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.limitations: Other strawberry leaf spots look similar; confirm locally if unsure.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot causes small dark spots on tomato leaves and fruit and spreads by splashing water and infected seed.

symptoms.name: Small dark spots
symptoms.explanation: Greasy dark spots, sometimes with yellow halos.

symptoms.name: Fruit scabs
symptoms.explanation: Raised, scabby spots on green fruit.

actions.step: Remove infected leaves and plant debris.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Avoid overhead watering and handling wet plants.
Use disease-free seed and rotate crops.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.monitoring: Check leaves every few days after rain.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.limitations: Several tomato spots look alike; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Leaf mould is a fungal disease common in humid greenhouses or dense plantings.

symptoms.name: Yellow patches
symptoms.explanation: Pale yellow patches on the upper leaf surface.

symptoms.name: Olive mould
symptoms.explanation: Olive-green to grey velvety growth on the leaf underside.

actions.step: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity.
Remove infected leaves.
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.monitoring: Check leaf undersides twice a week in humid conditions.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.limitations: Underside growth helps confirm; consult an expert if unsure.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot causes many small round spots on lower tomato leaves and spreads in wet weather.

symptoms.explanation: Many spots with grey centres and dark edges.

symptoms.name: Lower leaves first
symptoms.explanation: Starts on lower leaves; they yellow and drop.

actions.step: Remove and destroy badly affected leaves (do not compost).
actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.monitoring: Check lower leaves every few days after rain.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny pests that suck sap from leaves, multiplying fast in hot, dry weather.

symptoms.explanation: Tiny yellow or white dots on the leaf surface.

symptoms.name: Webbing
symptoms.explanation: Fine webs on the leaf underside in heavy infestations.

Remove heavily infested leaves.
Ask your extension office about miticides or beneficial predators.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.monitoring: Check leaf undersides with a hand lens twice a week in hot weather.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Target spot is a fungal disease causing brown spots with rings on tomato leaves, stems, and fruit in warm, humid weather.

symptoms.name: Ringed spots

symptoms.name: Leaf drop
symptoms.explanation: Spots merge and leaves drop from the bottom up.

actions.safety_note: Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.

actions.step: Improve airflow by pruning and spacing.
Use a fungicide only if your local extension office recommends one for this disease.
actions.safety_note: Follow label rates, protective gear, and pre-harvest intervals.

Tomato___Target_Spot.monitoring: Check lower and middle leaves weekly in humid weather.
Tomato___Target_Spot.limitations: Very similar to early blight; confirm with an expert if unsure.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus is spread by whiteflies and stunts plants. There is no cure for infected plants.

symptoms.name: Yellow edges

Use resistant varieties next season.
